status: Source implementation validated locally; not included in the published 0.10.1 archives or current production Worker.
change: Host process.execFile and built-in shell command dispatch resolve executable shebang chains to an installed WASI interpreter. Rust owns header parsing; Effect owns bounded R2 loading and admission into the existing immutable WASI program archive.

nativeProof.runtime: Native Alchemy workerd, R2 and Queue; Bun 1.4.3 on local Linux.
cases: Preserves optional argument containing spaces, nested script paths, caller argv, environment and binary stdin.
Four script levels execute; self-recursive interpretation fails ELOOP.
Relative interpreter path resolves against /home/cirro without PATH search.
Built-in shell pipeline dispatch preserves stdin and argv.
Missing/empty/non-executable interpreters reject admission; inserted arguments count against the 128-argument limit.
Execute-only capabilities cannot read scripts; another sandbox capability is denied.
Replacement Worker consumes the original captured interpreter, argv, environment and stdin after the script header changes.
nativeProof.publishedInterpreterTest: tests/published-shell.test.ts downloads the existing digest-pinned sh and jq packages, validates their exact size and SHA-256, then executes a shebang script through the real sh interpreter. The script observes argv/environment/stdin and writes a file that is read through the public filesystem API.

validation.completeGate: bun run check passed: runtime and SDK builds, TypeScript, workspace Clippy, Cargo tests and native Bun tests.
validation.rustParser: Header tests cover optional argument preservation, UTF-8, NUL, empty/plain inputs and the bounded header.

limits: At most four script levels and a header ending within 256 bytes; overlong headers are rejected rather than truncated.
Final interpreter must be WASI. No automatic interpreter installation, new JS/Python execFile runtime or complete Linux execve parity is claimed.
The interpreter binary and argv are captured before Queue execution. Script bodies remain filesystem reads performed by the interpreter, not immutable body snapshots.
WASI guest exec/fexec dispatch is unchanged; this increment covers host/agent process.execFile and the built-in shell boundary.
No new release archives, production deployment, remote binding proof or Minutei deployment in this increment.
Test duration is not a benchmark of production latency, throughput or cost.
